text:
lia: quick idea — instead of purely env-based TTLs, what if we anchor retention to alerts/incidents? keep traces that are referenced by alert rules or incident tickets in hot storage longer (90d) and everything else gets default 30d. this would reduce noise but keep high-signal traces for postmortems :thinking:

owen: interesting. do you mean "anchor" by a tag on the span like `incident.id` or by links from the alert system?

lia: either. two ways: 1) when an alert fires we attach alert.metadata (alert.id, rule) to the traces we sampled around that time; 2) any trace that gets explicitly linked from an incident ticket gets promoted. both should update an index so the storage tier knows to keep it.

sanjay: from the exporter side we could add an OTLP attribute enrichment pipeline to stamp `alert.anchor=true` when the alerting pipeline correlates spans. low risk. small perf hit for correlation step.

maria: curious about cost - hot storage is expensive. what's the ballpark delta if 5% of traces become anchored vs putting everything in 60d hot?

owen: rough estimate: hot cost ~ $0.02/trace-day (example). if we anchor 5% at 90d vs making all 100% at 60d, cost = 0.05*90 + 0.95*30 = 33.5 trace-days avg vs 60 if all warm-hot. so huge savings. i can run more precise numbers per service if desired.

lia: UX reqs for Console: add an "Alert-anchored retention" toggle per alert rule + default retention knobs per env. also surface count of currently anchored traces so users see impact.

kevin: operationally we need a GC flow: mark traces with `anchor_until` timestamp, GC ignores anchors until expiry. implement index in Dynamo (or ES) that maps alert_id -> trace_ids and a small background job to set anchor_until.

maria: any concerns about legal/compliance? some customers want 180d for prod traces regardless. we need per-customer overrides.

lia: yes, compliance override will be a hard cap. default policy: service/env default TTL, alert-anchored TTL (configurable), and customer-level minimum TTL. rollout: feature-flag in staging for one org first.

infra-bot: deploy:retention-indexer v0.3 deployed to staging (sha: ab12cd) — watcher enabled for alert->trace correlation :rocket:

kevin: code sketch for config that the console would generate:
```yaml
retention:
  default_ttl_days: 30
  alert_anchor_ttl_days: 90
  compliance_min_ttl_days: 180 # per-customer override
  anchor_labels: ["alert.id","incident.id","alert.rule"]
```

owen: one more thought — alarms/metrics should count anchored traces separately so SRE can see if an alert is causing retention churn. we should add a dashboard tile in Redwood Console and a cost estimate per-alert.

lia: agreed. next steps: owen can run cost sims per service, kevin will prototype anchor index + GC job, sanjay will add exporter enrichment hook. i'll draft a short Console UX mock and we can ship to staging.

maria: +1, schedule a 30m sync tomorrow?

lia: scheduled 10:30 PDT tomorrow. adding agenda: cost sims, indexing approach, and privacy overrides. :thumbsup:
